from: FR-2 (mgmt-pg), as contributed; case format fixed before landing — see notes below
appliesTo: every engine entry whose clock/types blocks are present, plus every entry in bindings
format: See verification/fixtures/README.md. Two mechanisms were added while landing this set and are explained there: `requires` can assert a capability is ABSENT (so a case can describe an engine that lacks it), and `expects: "reject"` lets a case assert a refusal instead of a result.

cases.why: a bound LIMIT/OFFSET slot is a BINDING fact: the statement text carries {ph}, which the runner renders from bindings.<name>.params
steps: SELECT 1 LIMIT {ph} OFFSET {ph}
assert: the engine accepts bound parameters in LIMIT/OFFSET slots

steps: SELECT {clock.serverNow} AS v
assert: the value matches the declared clock.valueType / precision / timezone:
valueType 'timestamp with time zone' -> microsecond precision, tz-aware
valueType 'text' -> 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', second precision, no tz
assert on the READING (typeof / pg_typeof), never on the spelling of the call

cases.why: the comparison must survive the declared valueType. `<=` is used rather than `>` so the case is deterministic across precisions: the stored value was taken before the query's own now.
steps: CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, expires_at {types.timestamptz})
INSERT INTO t (id, expires_at) VALUES (1, {clock.serverNow})
SELECT id FROM t WHERE expires_at <= {clock.serverNow}
assert: 1 row returned — the stored value and the query's now are comparable under the declared valueType

steps: CREATE TABLE ts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, at {types.timestamptz} NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
INSERT INTO ts (id) VALUES (1)
SELECT at FROM ts WHERE id = 1
assert: at is populated — DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP is the portable suffix, measured true on all three

steps: CREATE TABLE ts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, at {types.timestamptz} NOT NULL DEFAULT now())
assert: DEFAULT now() is accepted — postgres only

cases.why: the ABSENT half of the previous case. `equals: false` is what makes it run on exactly the engines that declare ddlDefaultNow false; a case that merely required the capability would SKIP there and assert nothing.
steps: CREATE TABLE ts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, at {types.timestamptz} NOT NULL DEFAULT now())
assert: the DDL is refused — DEFAULT now() is a syntax error where ddlDefaultNow is false

steps: CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, active {types.boolean})
INSERT INTO t (id, active) VALUES (1, TRUE)
SELECT active FROM t WHERE id = 1
assert: the value round-trips truthy — BOOLEAN natively on an enforcing engine

steps: CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, active {types.boolean})
INSERT INTO t (id, active) VALUES (1, TRUE)
SELECT active, typeof(active) AS ty FROM t
assert: active reads 1 with typeof 'integer' — affinity, not a boolean type (measured on sqlite and turso)

cases.why: the fail-closed rule does NOT apply where types.enforced is false, and this case proves the contract says so instead of pretending otherwise.
steps: CREATE TABLE z (a FLOOBLE)
assert: the DDL is accepted — affinity takes any type name, so there is nothing to refuse

steps: CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, doc {types.map.jsonb})
INSERT INTO t (id, doc) VALUES (1, '{"a":1}')
SELECT doc ->> 'a' AS v FROM t
assert: v is 1 — -> and ->> work on ALL THREE, including the embedded engines (measured)

steps: CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, doc {types.map.jsonb})
INSERT INTO t (id, doc) VALUES (1, '{"a":1}')
SELECT doc @> '{"a":1}' AS v FROM t
assert: @> is true — native jsonb

cases.why: the operator surface is where jsonb actually differs, not extraction. Asserting this keeps the difference from being over-stated the other way.
steps: CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, doc {types.map.jsonb})
INSERT INTO t (id, doc) VALUES (1, '{"a":1}')
SELECT doc @> '{"a":1}' AS v FROM t
assert: @> is refused — unrecognized token on the embedded engines

cases.why: binding-scoped: the affected-row and insert-id field NAMES come from bindings.<name>.result, never from the engine entry
steps: INSERT INTO t (id, name) VALUES (1, 'a')
assert: the driver's result carries the field named by result.affectedField
when result.insertIdField is null, an id must come back via RETURNING instead
assert the DECLARED name against the field the binding actually reports

steps: SELECT 1 AS {identifierQuote}weird name{identifierQuote}
assert: the quoted identifier round-trips, and a renderer emits only the declared quote character — never sqlite's legacy backtick or bracket forms

steps: {serverInfo}
assert: the declared query returns a version-shaped value

runnerObligation: Same as tx.json — a fresh database per case, and the `requires` check FIRST so a capability the engine lacks is SKIPPED, never failed. Additionally: resolve {ph} and every binding-scoped case against the `bindings` section, never against the engine; and honour `expects: 'reject'` by asserting that the statement is refused rather than by letting the error escape. A skip must be reported as a skip: 'cannot express it' and 'failed it' are different facts and only one is a defect.
